signals.content: 🇺🇸🇨🇳 The U.S. military is RACING for AI dominance, but internal feuds and China keep getting in the way... The Pentagon banned Anthropic’s AI from defense systems after the company’s CEO refused to let the military use it without restrictions on surveillance and autonomous weapons. Weeks later, contractors were told they could ignore the ban... for now. Meanwhile, China is closing the gap fast. American officials worry Beijing could be only MONTHS behind on the most powerful models. Sudden bans, sudden reversals, and a national-security establishment struggling to keep up with technology that is constantly evolving... The race is on... but the U.S. is grappling with problems that China just isn't. Source: NYT / Writer: Sol

signals.content: Eight months after its establishment, Project Maven had computer vision capability operating in combat, not a lab or a test environment, but in theater alongside deployed forces. The Pentagon's traditional acquisition process would have taken years. Maven's team bypassed it through continuous refinement shaped by operational feedback at every iteration. That approach earned trust the way military organizations actually earn trust: through mission performance. Full review from The Military Reading Room: https://t.co/sZXeM9Fse1
